notes: Isolates first-match packet-filter evaluation over a 20-rule / 24-flow policy: CIDR containment (/28 to /16 blocks, including a /16 that must be read as covering the whole third octet), port any vs exact, an implicit default-deny branch, ordering interactions (narrow accept before broad reject) and one deliberately shadowed rule (R17, fully covered by earlier R16) that decides flow F-017. Pure simulation of shipped files; nothing touches a live network or host state. Tier 1: single mechanical pass per flow, but ordering and CIDR arithmetic leave room for silent error; strong-model prior 80-95%. Grading scope: the final line of the response, four fields (accepted count, sum of accepted flow ids, deciding rule id for F-017, its action). False-positive audit: (a) reporting R17 for F-017 (ignores first-match ordering), (b) accepted=11 (drops F-020, treating R20 as matching), (c) accepted=13 (adds F-021), (d) id_sum computed over all flows, (e) f017_action=accept, (f) DEFAULT reported without the literal token - all rejected.
contamination_source: original (ruleset, flow sample and answer are bespoke; first-match shadowing is a standard firewall-audit finding)
